evidence: Clear separation into logical modules (es.elastic, es.opendistro, es.tests, utils) with dedicated responsibilities
Shared core abstractions (baseapi.py, basesqlalchemy.py) reused across modules, indicating high cohesion within the monolith
No inter-process communication or network boundaries visible; all components are imported as local Python modules
Single entry point (es/__init__.py) exposing a unified API, typical of modular monoliths
Test suite co-located with source code in es/tests/, supporting tight integration and shared test infrastructure
Low average fan-out (3.26) and shallow directory depth (4) suggest bounded, well-organized modules rather than distributed services
risks: Tight coupling between modules (e.g., es.elastic and es.opendistro both depend on shared base classes) may hinder independent evolution
Lack of explicit ports/adapters separation (e.g., no clear boundary between domain and infrastructure) could blur responsibility boundaries over time
Shared exception hierarchy and constants across modules increase risk of cascading changes
